vulnerability_analysis: The $xenox contract has owner-only functions that can be abused to extract funds: 1) setdevAddress() allows the owner to set any address as the dev wallet, 2) setBuydevFeePercent()/setSelldevFeePercent() allow setting dev fees to arbitrary values, 3) transferTokens() allows the owner to directly transfer any tokens from the contract balance to any address, 4) swapAndLiquify() sends accumulated BNB and tokens to the dev address. The owner can abuse these privileges to drain contract funds.
attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank(), then: 1) Set attacker address as the dev address via setdevAddress(), 2) Call transferTokens() to drain any tokens held by the contract to attacker, 3) If there's BNB in the contract, it will be sent to dev address during swapAndLiquify. The oracle checks if attacker's NATIVE balance increased, so we need to ensure BNB extraction.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the contract owner address via owner() view function, 2. Record initial attacker BNB balance, 3. Impersonate owner with vm.startPrank(owner), 4. Call setdevAddress() to set attacker as dev, 5. Call transferTokens() to drain tokens (if any), 6. Stop prank, 7. Verify attacker balance increased via assertGt
